correctness.rationale: The minimal nonfaces are precisely the pairwise-intersecting triples of distinct two-subsets (stars or triangles). I independently used this characterization to enumerate all faces, and used coface-first matching rather than the frozen coreduction program. The three full oriented Hasse DAGs have respectively 232, 159, 72 faces; 720, 471, 168 covers; 111, 77, 33 matched pairs; and critical counts {0:1,3:9}, {0:1,3:4}, {0:1,2:5}. The acyclic-matching theorem therefore gives the asserted wedges: with one vertex and just one positive cell dimension, the attaching maps are constant. The S5 action on two-subsets transports the computation to every vertex. The relative chain complex of (K,D_v) is the augmented link chain complex shifted by one, by removing v from each surviving simplex (with v oriented first). Thus the pair sequence gives exactly 0 -> Z^4 -> Z^9 -> Z^5 -> 0 over Z; the free quotient makes the image primitive and gives a noncanonical splitting. The ranks describe the image and quotient, not recovery of four distinguished basis elements. value.rationale: Petersen is a canonical nonbipartite test for a graph complex studied on bipartite families. Knowing the ambient nine classes does not tell what survives a vertex failure; the exact local wedge types and primitive rank-four image distinguish local loss of five free classes from possible torsion or different local topology. The classification is uniform for every vertex and useful at its finite scale, without claims about multiple punctures, particular generators, or equivariant splittings.
